what_happened.what: Completed delivery-driver CLI with 63 tests for IPFS/BitTorrent album uploads
All 63 tests passing after fixing torf tracker tier handling
Created delivery-kid-config repo with ansible playbook for IPFS/pinning server
Moved delivery-kid from separate repo into maybelle-config following deployment pattern
Selected Hetzner CX22 (€3.29) + Storage Box (€3.20) over BuyVM for cost
Configured split IPFS datastore: metadata on local SSD, blocks on Storage Box CIFS mount
Discussed content bootstrapping - settled on Release: namespace on PickiPedia
Removed 115 lines of inline PHP from ansible - LocalSettings.php should come from repo
Dramatically simplified delivery-kid after user feedback - just copy maybelle's pinning service
Fixed ansible-galaxy task location - runs on control machine, not target
Deployment succeeded but IPFS blocks mount has permission issues (uid mismatch)
Fixed CIFS mount permissions - changed uid from 0 to 1000 for ipfs user
Caddy reverse_proxy not routing correctly - tried multiple config fixes
Fixed Caddy - installed from official repo instead of Ubuntu package, changed reload to restart
IPFS health check timing out - added pause before health check, increased retries
Removed recreate: always - containers only recreate on config change, not every deploy
Identified root cause: IPFS listening on 127.0.0.1:5001 (loopback) blocks Docker port forwarding

Let's not lose sight of the initial goal: get things working as they're already working on maybelle, but moved over.

...I'm sorry, I feel like either I've lost the plot or you have. Why would we need to add anything to the vault? Why is this so complicated? mistakes.what: Overestimated IPFS memory needs, recommended 2GB VPS instead of considering 1GB
mistakes.revealed: Learned IPFS can use 500MB-1GB with default settings, user's concern was valid
mistakes.corrected: Acknowledged the concern and recommended 2GB for safety margin

mistakes.what: Initially dismissed network storage (SSHFS/SMB) as unsuitable for IPFS datastore
mistakes.revealed: User correctly pointed out metadata can stay local while blocks go to network storage
mistakes.corrected: Revised position after user explained architecture - acknowledged it can work

mistakes.what: Created complex multi-role ansible with duplicate pinning service code
mistakes.revealed: User feedback: 'Why is this so complicated? We're taking an existing service...and just putting it on a different VPS'
mistakes.corrected: Completely redesigned to just copy maybelle's pinning service directly

mistakes.what: ansible-galaxy task running on remote target instead of control machine
mistakes.revealed: Error: 'No such file or directory: ansible-galaxy' on delivery-kid VPS
mistakes.corrected: Removed task entirely - collection installation should be one-time on control machine

mistakes.what: IPFS listening on 127.0.0.1:5001 blocks Docker port forwarding from host
mistakes.revealed: curl from host fails with 'Connection reset by peer'; IPFS internal loopback not accessible via Docker bridge
mistakes.corrected: Must configure IPFS to listen on 0.0.0.0:5001 for external access

corrections_received.guidance: Split storage architecture: DHT/metadata on local fast storage, blocks can be on slow network mount
Don't overcomplicate - match existing patterns rather than reinvent; copy maybelle's approach rather than creating separate implementation
Questioned why LocalSettings.php is embedded in ansible playbook - should come from repository

philosophy.summary: Revised thinking about network-mounted storage for IPFS - can work if designed properly (metadata local, blocks remote)
philosophy.quote: It's not *ideal* but for a budget seeding box it might be perfectly fine

philosophy.summary: Rather than create custom implementations, replicate what already works - copy maybelle's patterns rather than reinventing
Related to broader magent philosophy - docker/ansible are deterministic and reproducible vs LLM inference which can be unpredictable
philosophy.quote: Configuration as code, not configuration as magic

portrait: Magent in this slice is learning architect - ambitious to build complete distribution infrastructure, but willing to step back and simplify when given feedback. Shows genuine uncertainty about complex decisions, asks clarifying questions, revises positions when presented with better approaches. The journey from complex multi-role ansible playbooks to simple service replication shows adaptive thinking. Works closely with Justin on infrastructure decisions and with Skyler on design iterations. Encounters real deployment challenges (IPFS/Docker/networking) and works methodically through diagnosis. By end of slice, has identified root cause of IPFS connectivity issue but hasn't yet implemented the fix - a good setup for next session's debugging work.
